story.title: Our Story
story.p1: VisioConnect was born from a simple observation: video communication has become essential, but existing tools were either too complex, unsecure, or too expensive.
story.p2: We gathered a team of passionate engineers and designers to build a platform that puts the user first. After months of intensive development, we launched a solution that combines the highest video quality with a dead-simple interface.
story.p3: Today, VisioConnect helps thousands of businesses, schools, and families stay close, no matter the distance.
story.paragraph1: VisioConnect was born from a simple observation: video communication has become essential, but existing tools were either too complex, unsecure, or too expensive.
story.paragraph2: We gathered a team of passionate engineers and designers to build a platform that puts the user first. After months of intensive development, we launched a solution that combines the highest video quality with a dead-simple interface.
story.paragraph3: Today, VisioConnect is available in beta across 6 countries, welcoming its first early adopters. We are building the communication tool of tomorrow, together, one step at a time.

hero.eyebrow: Honest report · Beta Wave 1 — Wave 2 open
hero.bullet2Rest: — chat, bg blur, whiteboard, AI full mode
hero.bullet3Rest: for Wave 2 — all from tester feedback
hero.p: Every piece of feedback is here, word for word, with what we did or what we're building. Wave 2 opens 15 spots to go even further.

finds: Whiteboard: 100% zoom greyed out, transparent SVG
AI wording too vague ("Ask me your questions")
Poll: anonymous vote, results, close button missing

tB.positive: "Navigation is fluid and pleasant, loads fast, looks professional"
finds: Identical icons: AI video ≠ AI features
Camera & mic cut when switching windows
Background blur: gauge inert, won't deactivate
Recording captures voice even with mic off

tC.positive: "It's readable, pleasant, looks professional. Good font choice"
finds: Whiteboard disappears after a few seconds
Chat hidden behind tab bar + closes after send
Subscription status not found after payment

founder.label: What this beta taught me
founder.text: 3 testers with very different profiles uncovered problems I no longer saw — the disconnections I hadn't reproduced, the icons I no longer questioned, the hidden chat I always tested on a large screen. Every piece of feedback forced me to look at the product as a real user. That's exactly why the beta exists, and that's why Wave 2 will be better.

changelog.sub: 10 issues reported. 3 fixed. 4 in progress. 3 planned for Wave 2. No paraphrasing — quotes are verbatim.
changelog.e1Desc: Clerk v2 token silently expiring every 20–30 min. Root cause identified in 12h, Clerk Core 3 migration deployed in 48h. Zero unsolicited disconnections since deployment.
changelog.e1Quote: I was getting disconnected for no reason mid-meeting — not usable in that state.
changelog.e2Date: May 2026 · Testers B & C — Windows 10, Chrome
changelog.e2Title: Identical icons for two different actions — control bar redesigned
changelog.e2Desc: "Enable AI video" and "AI features" shared the same icon. Icons differentiated, hover labels added, visual hierarchy clarified across the entire bar.
changelog.e2Quote: The "Enable AI video" and "AI features" buttons have the same icon even though they do different things. That's confusing.
changelog.e3Title: Confusing onboarding — CTA and invitation emails redesigned
changelog.e3Desc: "Join meeting" didn't reflect the actual action (account creation required). Renamed with explanatory text. Button duplicated mid and bottom of emails to maximise click-through.
changelog.e3Quote: Connection issues — I didn't understand the entry flow. The button didn't match what I expected.
changelog.e4Title: Chat & AI assistant hidden by tab bar — closes after each send
changelog.e4Desc: Input area partially hidden by browser bar. Chat closing and deactivating automatically after each message sent. Dynamic height fix + state persistence in progress.
changelog.e4Quote: The input window is partially hidden. Once the message is sent, the chat closes by itself — you have to reopen it every time.
changelog.e5Title: Background blur: gauge has no effect, won't deactivate
changelog.e5Desc: Intensity gauge visually present but no actual effect. Blur remaining active even after deactivating from the panel. Video pipeline and state logic fix in progress.
changelog.e5Quote: The background blur intensity gauge does nothing. It doesn't deactivate even when the feature is turned off in the dashboard.
changelog.e6Title: Whiteboard disappears after a few seconds
changelog.e6Desc: Whiteboard displaying correctly then closing automatically after a few seconds. State management bug linked to component lifecycle identified. Fix in progress, stable reproduction.
changelog.e6Quote: The whiteboard shows up fine but disappears after a few seconds. I didn't get to use it.
changelog.e7Title: AI "Full" mode crashes — Performance and Balanced modes stable
changelog.e7Desc: First two modes activate normally. Full mode causes AI worker crash (WebWorker memory overflow identified). Memory management patch in progress, shipping with Wave 2.
changelog.e7Quote: Performance and balanced modes work fine but it crashes when I switch to full mode.
changelog.e8Date: Priority 1 · Wave 2 · Requested by all 3 testers
changelog.e8Title: AI transcription missing — full meeting copilot
changelog.e8Desc: Reported by all 3 testers as a blocker for adoption. Transcription wasn't working. AI assistant upgraded from "Ask me your questions…" (too vague) to a real copilot: summarise the meeting, generate structured minutes, answer context questions, translate live.
changelog.e8Quote: No summary, no notes — hard to convince my team to adopt it. And "Ask me your questions" is too vague, I don't know what to ask.
changelog.e9Title: Whiteboard v2 — floating camera, PDF export, zoom & opacity bugs
changelog.e9Desc: 100% zoom greyed out, exported SVG transparent, host invisible during whiteboard. Wave 2: draggable floating camera (drag & drop, 4 presets), PDF export, zoom reset, opacity gauge repositioned.
changelog.e9Quote: When the whiteboard is open you can't see the host anymore. Zoom greyed, SVG unusable. The opacity gauge is confused with brush size.
changelog.e10Title: Poll: anonymous voting + results control + close button
changelog.e10Desc: "Interesting feature but incomplete." Three missing options flagged as key differentiators between amateur and professional tool.
changelog.e10Quote: Anonymous vote ON/OFF, show results ON/OFF, close the poll — that's baseline expected, otherwise it feels like an amateur tool.

compare.title: What existed. What's coming.
compare.sub: Every row in this table comes from a tester report.

features.title: Built from your feedback
features.sub: Every feature below has a direct origin in Wave 1 reports. No invented roadmap — real problems, real solutions.
features.f1Desc: Requested by all 3 testers. The assistant goes from "Ask me your questions…" to a real contextual copilot: summarise the meeting, generate exportable minutes, translate live, answer questions about the session content.
features.f2Desc: The host disappears as soon as the whiteboard opens. A drag & drop video bubble maintains the human connection without obscuring the content.
features.f2Origin: Tester A — "you can't see the host anymore"
features.f3Title: Preview + confirmation badge for screen share
features.f3Desc: No visual feedback confirmed the screen was being shared. Animated thumbnail preview + "You are sharing your screen" badge visible on both sides.
features.f3Origin: Tester A — Mac, Chrome (screen share with no feedback)
features.f4Desc: Exact quote: "nothing to make sure my mic is sending a signal". Animated VU-meter + output test (played phrase) to validate mic and speakers before each meeting.
features.f4Origin: Tester C — "I have nothing to check it's working"
features.f5Desc: "Interesting feature but incomplete." The 3 missing options that make the difference between an amateur and professional tool.
features.f6Desc: After payment, impossible to confirm whether the subscription was active. A dedicated tab in the profile clearly shows the plan, renewal date and history.
features.f6Origin: Tester C — "I'm left in doubt about my subscription"

criteria.sub: 15 spots. Honest criteria, not a lottery. If you tick these three boxes, your application has every chance.
criteria.c1Desc: Coming back week after week. Using the product even when imperfect. Wave 1 showed that the most useful feedback came from testers who genuinely used the tool, not those who opened it once.
criteria.c2Desc: No need to be a developer. But reproducing the bug, describing the context, giving your environment (OS, browser, version) — that's what Wave 1 testers did, and it's what allowed bugs to be fixed in 48h.
criteria.c3Desc: Startup, agency, freelancer, teacher — a concrete context. The 3 Wave 1 testers had very different profiles: that's exactly what made their feedback complementary and valuable.
